body.x: Electrical-stimulation care devices commonly rely on adhesive electrode pads that have to be placed on the skin before each use, which makes them awkward to use on the neck, shoulders, arms and legs.
EVON's PICON takes the pads out of the process.

EVON Corporation, a Daegu-based healthcare solutions company established in 2021 and led by CEO Hocheol Shin, is exhibiting PICON at KES 2026, along with its companion Booster Gel. PICON is a portable myofascial care device that uses EMS and TENS low-frequency microcurrent technology and a patented multi-contact, three-dimensional curved aluminum head designed to keep stable contact across different parts of the body.

The device weighs about 130 g and offers four care modes and five intensity levels, and it works without adhesive electrode pads. Booster Gel is a cosmetic product developed to improve contact between skin and electrode and to make application smoother. PICON has KC, CE and FCC certifications, and EVON maintains an ISO 9001-certified quality management system. The product has also received a PIN UP Design Award.

EVON says PICON has sold about 6,000 units since launch, for cumulative sales of about KRW 1 billion (about USD 710,000), and that it ran three successful crowdfunding campaigns on Wadiz. In Korea, it sells through its official online store, Naver Smart Store, Coupang and Hyundai Mall, as well as personal training studios, fitness centers and wellness facilities.

After its first export to Hong Kong, the company is in discussions with buyers and distributors in Japan, India, Taiwan, Vietnam, Australia, the Czech Republic and other markets. It regards Japan and other Asian markets as strategic because of demand for Korean healthcare and beauty products and their proximity, and plans to expand gradually into the United States and Europe. EVON is seeking importers, distributors and master distributors as well as partners in healthcare, sports, wellness and beauty, and is open to local distribution, joint marketing and OEM and ODM collaboration.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
